look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: a cool-season winter ANNUAL with opposite heart/triangular SCALLOPED leaves, the upper ones CROWDED into a reddish-purple pointed top. Follow an UPPER leaf all the way to the stem: it retains a SHORT PETIOLE and DOES NOT form a stalkless collar. Henbit L. amplexicaule instead has rounded/lobed SESSILE upper leaves encircling the stem; both make pink-purple two-lipped flowers on square stems. Purple color varies with light/stage and is NOT diagnostic by itself.
taxonomy_notes: POWO accepted Lamium purpureum L., not a henbit synonym; may include different infraspecific concepts but this learner card does not identify varieties.

project_inclusion.source_pool: User approved adding the henbit look-alike as its own card
project_inclusion.notes: POWO confirms species introduced in Texas and native to Europe/western Asia/Med. Not a native restoration recommendation; no official Texas invasive designation asserted.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Cool-season herbaceous winter annual with shallow roots and square stems often rooting at low nodes.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Opposite at stem nodes, prominently crenate/scalloped; lower foliage broadly ovate/heart shaped and petiolate.
morphology_keys.upper_leaf: Upper leaves short-stalked (PETIOLATE), crowded, more triangular/pointed, often distinctly purplish. Unlike henbit the bases don't form complete green stem-clasping collars; examine from below when top leaves overlap.
morphology_keys.flowers: Clusters (verticillasters) at upper nodes; pink-purple tubular two-lipped flowers, upper hood and patterned lower lip with pollen-bearing stamens.
morphology_keys.stem: Four-angled, often purplish near nodes; hairs can be sparse; cross-section is a mint FAMILY clue, not species-only proof.
morphology_keys.fruits: Four little nutlets develop within persistent calyx; mature nutlet/fruit macro not yet available.
morphology_keys.habitat: Disturbed winter-spring open ground, turf margins, beds, fields and paths; it is introduced and can provide nectar without constituting native host-plant support.

comparisons.key_distinctions: PURPUREUM: pointed purple-tinged upper leaves with short PETIOLES; AMPLEXICAULE: green round/lobed upper leaves SESSILE/clasping. Both may have purplish blooms and square stems. Glechoma creeps as perennial and retains petioles to flowers.

field_matrix.quick_rule: Upper leaves retain short stalks and cluster into pointed often-purple cap
field_matrix.flower_position: Pink bilabiate flowers partly tucked among compact purple upper leaves

field_matrix.quick_rule: Upper leaves are sessile rounded/lobed collars on stem
field_matrix.flower_position: Long projecting purple tubes rising above green upper collars

field_matrix.quick_rule: Creeping perennial, stolons and stalked rounded leaves near flower
field_matrix.flower_position: Broader purple flowers in leaf axils

not_reliable_alone: A purple top is common but may be faint or missing.
Square stems/opposite leaves establish mint-family resemblance, not exact species.
Young rosettes lack fully developed upper flowering nodes.
Close petioles may be hidden beneath dense purple top foliage.

visual_comparison.title: Purple deadnettle — top leaves, petioles and the henbit split
visual_comparison.subtitle: FOUR physically installed, individually licensed L. purpureum photographs now all have checked anatomy arrows, plus one explicit henbit other-species comparison. The densely crowded pointed purple upper leaf cap and corolla hood/calyx are photo-proven; upper short petiole insertion and ripe four-nutlet fruits are still missing true macros.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: PURPLE POINTED UPPER CAP + SHORT PETIOLES = PURPLE DEADNETTLE. ROUND SESSILE GREEN COLLARS = HENBIT.

items.why_it_matters: The upper triangular purple leaf cap suggests purple deadnettle; trace a SHORT PETIOLE to distinguish it confidently from henbit's sessile green collar.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Purple deadnettle: photograph the cap, then check the leaf stalk
steps: First locate the often purplish pointed upper leaf cap and greener scalloped lower leaves.
Zoom into the true flower macro for hairy upper lip, lower lip, and green calyx teeth.
LIFT an upper pointed leaf in the field to find a SHORT PETIOLE. Neither the current photos nor mere purple coloration independently proves this stalk.
Compare with HENBIT: rounded green sessile upper collar; use several mature nodes, not a young rosette.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: PURPLE POINTED CAP + actual short-stalked upper leaf + hooded corolla suggests L. purpureum. Henbit upper leaves are rounded and sessile/clasping.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Four physical exact species images, but a TRUE exposed upper petiole junction and mature fruit/nutlets are still missing. No fake anatomical arrows.

Fresh open flower front/side showing hood, lower spotted corolla, stamens

Paired henbit stalkless green collar versus deadnettle short stalk on same photo scale
